name: Nook
description:
Your smart home from the top bar. Switch lights and fans, read the sensors, see what is online, watch and turn cameras, run air conditioners, control TVs and speakers.

Works with Home Assistant, Philips Hue bridges and HomeKit accessories, and with Smart Life (Tuya), Mi Home and eWeLink accounts: Home Assistant by an access token, Hue by the button on the bridge, HomeKit by the setup code on the accessory, Smart Life and Mi Home by a QR code scanned with their app, eWeLink through its own sign-in page. On the local network it talks to Gree air conditioners, Tapo cameras, Sonoff switches in DIY mode and Cast speakers. TVs from Samsung, LG, Sony, Panasonic, Philips, Roku, Android and Google TV, and Apple TV are found on the network and paired the way each one asks, by a code or a prompt on its screen; the card shows the app or channel that is on and holds the volume, the inputs, the apps and a remote. Pairing an Android TV needs the openssl command.

Nook talks to the clouds of Mi Home, eWeLink and Smart Life the way their apps do: when the menu opens, and every few minutes for sensors shown in the top bar, never while the screen is locked.

Events of the sensors behind a Xiaomi gateway, a leak or smoke above all, become notifications the moment they happen, heard from the gateway itself on the local network. That is why Nook stays on while the screen is locked: listening to the gateway is all it does there, with no menu and no cloud.
